sections.presenting_complaint: Flare of rheumatoid arthritis for 3 weeks.
sections.history: Painful swelling of the right wrist and right hand knuckles for 3 weeks. Early morning stiffness lasting about 90 minutes (initially said 30 minutes). Mild foot ache. Mild nausea the day after methotrexate. No sore throat, fever, bruising, cough or breathlessness. Husband had shingles last month; patient had chickenpox as a child and has not had shingles.
sections.medications_allergies: Methotrexate 15 mg once daily. Folic acid 5 mg once weekly (Thursdays). Sulfadiazine: rash.
sections.examination: Synovitis of the left wrist and left 2nd and 3rd MCP joints. Right hand normal. Bloods: CRP 28, FBC and LFTs normal. DAS28 4.8.
sections.impression: Rheumatoid arthritis flare, moderate disease activity on methotrexate.
sections.plan: Increase methotrexate to 20 mg once weekly (Mondays); continue folic acid 5 mg once weekly (Thursdays). Intramuscular methylprednisolone 120 mg today. Bloods every 2 weeks for 6 weeks, then 3-monthly. Clinic review in 3 months.
sections.safety_netting: If sore throat, fever, mouth ulcers, unusual bruising or bleeding, or new cough or breathlessness: stop methotrexate, get an urgent blood test and call the rheumatology helpline. Report a painful blistering rash promptly.
